title: When the Extraction Wakes
premise: Vesper Galloway, a sleepless private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed their team, is approached by a stranger named Ilse who claims Vesper once saved her life — a favor Vesper has no memory of. Ilse's debt comes due when she reveals she carries the encryption key to 'Meridian,' a black-site program that turns private contractors into deniable weapons, and both the agency that built it and the syndicate trying to buy it want her dead. As Vesper and Ilse go on the run with Vesper's ragtag crew of misfit operators, they uncover that the incident that broke Vesper was Meridian's first field test — and that Vesper's missing memories hold the second half of the key. In the end, Vester must choose between restoring their own erased past and destroying Meridian forever, trading the secret worth killing for to save the found family they never expected to have.
about_author: August Iversen is a former maritime security consultant who spent a decade writing risk assessments before turning to fiction. They live off-grid on the Norwegian coast, where they write at night, allegedly because they still can't sleep.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Insomnia-ridden and medicating on coffee and routine, Vesper guards a paranoid tech executive through another meaningless night. A stranger, Ilse, intercepts them afterward claiming Vesper saved her in Tallinn three years ago — an event Vesper cannot recall. She leaves a burner phone: 'When you remember, call.' The beat is unease: someone knows something about Vesper's blank years.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The burner rings: Ilse is cornered in a dockside hotel by men with contractor training. Vesper goes alone, tells themselves it's curiosity, and pulls her out of an ambush that's too professional to be random. Ilse reveals she's carrying something everyone wants. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Crew You Keep
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse meets Vesper's skeleton crew — Dez the forger, Marisol the comms ghost, old Tomás who runs the safehouse — and realizes this broken little family is Vesper's real armor. The syndicate's hunters hit the safehouse; the crew scatters with Ilse. Beat: found family forming under fire, trust extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ilse explains: Meridian is a program implanting behavioral overrides into contract operatives, erasing missions from their own minds. Vesper's dead team were test subjects; Vesper's amnesia around Tallinn isn't trauma — it's a wipe. Beat: horror and grief reframed; the incident wasn't Vesper's failure, it was done to them.

chapters.title: What the Agency Buried
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez forges access into a decommissioned records vault and finds Vesper's name on the Meridian roster — listed as a success. Meanwhile Marisol intercepts word that the buying syndicate has a mole inside the crew. Beat: paranoia blooms; the family's foundation cracks as loyalty gets tested.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol traces the leak to Tomás, who sold them out to pay for his daughter's medical debts — and to guarantee the syndicate spares the crew. Confrontation at a rail yard turns violent; Tomás dies passing Vesper the syndicate's meeting location. Beat: betrayal, forgiveness too late, the cost of power over desperate people.

chapters.title: Half a Key
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Cornered by the agency's cleaner, Calloway, Ilse admits her half of the encryption key is biologically locked — it lives in her blood, and extracting it kills her. Vesper realizes the other half is buried in their own wiped memory. Beat: love against duty crystallizes; each would burn their half rather than let the other be used.

chapters.title: The House That Built Me
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. To recover the memory, Vesper voluntarily submits to a captured Meridian interface at an abandoned clinic — risking the same override that destroyed their team. Inside the wipe they relive Tallinn: they did save Ilse, then chose to forget to survive. Beat: climax of identity; Vesper wakes holding the full key and knowing exactly what it costs.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the handoff, Vesper offers the complete key to Calloway and the syndicate broker simultaneously — then triggers Marisol's deadman broadcast, exposing Meridian's client list to every government and press outlet alive. Firefight, sacrifice, Dez wounded shielding Ilse. Beat: the secret traded not for money or safety, but for its destruction.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Weeks later, hearings ripple outward while the crew hides in plain sight, rebuilding the security business on honest terms. Vesper sleeps eight hours straight for the first time since the incident and wakes to find the crew didn't stand guard — they trusted the world to leave them be. Final beat: quiet resolution; duty released, family kept.
